digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI / Gerrit Verified workflow
propositions: Ubuntu Verified jobs occupy 30.2 runner-minutes per change due to redundant YAML parsing, full-corpus Pandoc rendering, and inefficient fixture setup, driving queue contention on shared org runners without lossy coverage reduction.

Bridge cadence test re-parses 1440-minute workflow schedule inside exhaustive arithmetic loop; hoisting the parse operation to one-time pre-test load eliminates ~100s per cell without changing any checked minute or assertion.

Pandoc hardening suite runs both live-conversion and legacy-conversion subprocesses for all 884 units but verifies only legacy-to-baseline equality; replacing the 883 redundant legacy subprocesses with static immutable expected outputs eliminates subprocess overhead while preserving all 884 real product-conversion boundaries.

AST provenance fixture discovers caller/parent relationships by repeated tree traversal; pre-indexing these relationships at fixture setup eliminates ~48s per Ubuntu cell without changing any assertion or tuple.

Gerrit Verified workflow uses job-level always() predicates that block cancellation of superseded patchsets, causing 24+ minute stale-run admission delays when a replacement patchset arrives; switching to !cancelled() with existing classifier-failure fallback eliminates the serialization without removing assertions.

Individual test and operation durations on Ubuntu dropped from 34m26s to under 30 minutes on average through consensus-backed remediations that landed coverage-equivalent behavior: singleton repo_policy routing, isolated build fixtures, and static Pandoc oracle moving full corpus to scheduled External Integration.
